text:
Nisha: Heads-up — weird one: my ~100yo brass lamp (yes, vintage) seems to be killing my home Wi‑Fi every ~25–40 mins. Router sits on my desk. Anyone seen interference from old dimmer lamps? pic attached.
Samir: Oh no :grimacing: dimmer circuits and Wi‑Fi can be noisy. Is it a rotary dimmer?
Jordan: If it's an old incandescent dimmer it could create broadband noise. Can you try unplugging lamp for a while and see if drops stop?
Nisha: unplugged for 30m, no drops. plugged back in — drops after ~12 min. So 0->1 correlation. It's got a triac dimmer knob.
Nisha: dmesg shows wlan0 disconnects, here's a snippet: `wlan0: deauthenticating by local choice (reason=3)` — not sure that's useful.
Olivia: Is the router on the same power strip? Maybe the mains noise is coupling. Try moving router to different outlet and/or use an outlet strip with EMI filter.
Samir: Ferrite beads on the power cable helped me before. Also try moving router 1–2ft away and keep lamp on different circuit if possible.
Nisha: Great tips. Also tried moving to another outlet across the room (same breaker) and it still dropped. Will test a different circuit tomorrow.
Jordan: If you want a quick experiment: run `sudo iw dev wlan0 scan` continuously and tail to see AP disappear, or capture with phone hotspot to confirm it's local drop.
Nisha: Thanks — running a simple loop now: `while true; do sudo iw dev wlan0 scan | grep -i ssid; sleep 5; done`
Olivia: Also — measurable silver lining: lamp photos very 200% cozier than the outages. Would love to see a pic :eyes: 
Nisha: uploaded image (2.1 MB) — antique brass globe over ficus. lighting = cinematic.
Samir: beautiful. maybe call it 'the mood router killer' :smile:
deploy-bot: Heads-up: scheduled ISP firmware update tonight at 02:00, might be unrelated.
Jordan: FYI if it is triac dimmer interference you can add an RC snubber or a proper dimmer replacement (electronic dimmers are cleaner) — but that’s electrician territory.
Nisha: Thanks team. Next steps: borrow ferrite, test on separate circuit, maybe buy EMI filter. Will post results and lamp pics of my ficus glory.
